Subject: Request: extended handback window + subprocessor export

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and engineering have a couple of follow-ups on the retention/backup side before we finalize the DPA:

1) For regulated trial data we need a 90-day buffer after a customer-initiated delete to allow for downstream reconciliation with our data lake. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a "handback" window that delays backup purge for a named tenant by up to 90 days, and what controls are available to scope that to a single account?

2) Please provide the current subprocessor export (CSV) and an attest to whether any backup copies are stored outside the customer-controlled region (we need a list of any cross-border backups and the subprocessors involved).

3) We also have a one-off request: preserve the last 30 days of application logs (not PII) for a specific tenant ID while we complete a forensic review. We'd like an exception request template and an estimated ETA to complete the preservation and then purge.

I've attached a short PDF from legal outlining their DPA redline asks and a sample CSV with the fields we'd expect in the subproc export.

Can you route this internally and let us know next steps? We prefer to get a written confirmation for procurement.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Security & Privacy
BlueCove Therapeutics

Hi Maya —

Thanks — and thanks for the clear checklist. We're able to support scoped handback windows and a temporary log hold in most cases; I wanted to loop in Kim (legal) and Karthik (privacy/compliance) to confirm the DPA language and the mechanics for a tenant-scoped backup purge delay. Quick summary of what we can do and next steps: 

- Scoped handback: We can implement a tenant-level retention exception that delays automatic backup purge for up to 90 days. There are two implementation flavors: operator-enabled hold (Redwood ops does the hold for a customer) or customer-triggered hold via an API endpoint we can provision. Both are auditable and reversible.

- Subprocessor export: I will export the current subproc list and scrub contact details where required. I'll include storage region and whether backups are replicated cross-border.

- Log preservation: We can carve a 30-day preservation for application logs (non-PII) for a single tenant; we will require a signed exception form and an estimated completion date for the forensic review.

Action items: 
1) Kim/Karthik — please confirm whether the operator-enabled handback needs a legal annex (DPA amendment) or if an SOC2-backed operational process plus a signed exception form suffices.
2) I'll attach the exported subproc CSV and an internal runbook fragment describing the purge flow and rollback options.
3) Maya — can you confirm the tenant ID and the target completion date for the log preservation?

We'll aim to provide an export and an initial draft exception form by EOD tomorrow (Tue). If you'd like a quick call to walk through the controls, I'm available Tue afternoon.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference

Maya / Connor —

Short answer: we should do a narrow DPA amendment for the 90-day handback and a short, signed exception template for the log preservation. Rationale: operator-enabled holds that extend backup life are reasonably material because they change data lifecycle guarantees; procurement will want explicit contract-level language.

Proposed path: 
- I will draft a 1-paragraph amendment that: (a) allows tenant-scoped temporary retention exceptions up to 90 days; (b) requires written request from an authorized customer contact; (c) states Redwood will log and notify the customer of any cross-border replication associated with that tenant's backups.
- For log preservation, use the exception form (simple approvals + ETA + scope). We'll attach the form to the amendment as an exhibit in case you want both in one package.

Privacy note for Karthik: please confirm whether we need to involve the Subprocessor team for re-authorization for any cross-border backup stores that are not already covered by our DPA.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
